When [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled, route segment configs like `dynamic`, `revalidate`, and `fetchCache` are replaced by [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife).

The migration is driven by **instant navigation validation**. With Cache Components enabled, Next.js validates in development whether navigating into each route renders instantly, and surfaces the code that would block it as an error or insight.

The `use cache` directive allows you to mark a route, React component, or a function as cacheable. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file should be cached, or inline at the top of a function or component to cache the return value. Functions and components that use `use cache` must be async.

00002| title: cookies
00003| description: API Reference for the cookies function.
00004| ---
00005| 
00006| `cookies` is an **async** function that allows you to read the HTTP incoming request cookies in [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components), and read/write outgoing request cookies in [Server Functions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
00007| 
00008| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
00009| import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
00010| 
00011| export default async function Page() {
00012|   const cookieStore = await cookies()
00013|   const theme = cookieStore.get('theme')
00014|   return '...'
00015| }
00016| ```
00017| 
00018| ```js filename="app/page.js" switcher
00019| import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
00020| 
00021| export default async function Page() {
00022|   const cookieStore = await cookies()
00023|   const theme = cookieStore.get('theme')
00024|   return '...'
00025| }
00026| ```
00027| 
00028| ## Reference
00029| 
00030| ### Methods
00031| 
00032| The following methods are available:
00033| 
00034| | Method                      | Return Type      | Description                                                                     |
00035| | --------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
00036| | `get('name')`               | Object           | Accepts a cookie name and returns an object with the name and value.            |
00037| | `getAll()`                  | Array of objects | Returns a list of all the cookies with a matching name.                         |
00038| | `has('name')`               | Boolean          | Accepts a cookie name and returns a boolean based on if the cookie exists.      |
00039| | `set(name, value, options)` | -                | Accepts a cookie name, value, and options and sets the outgoing request cookie. |
00040| | `delete(name)`              | -                | Accepts a cookie name and deletes the cookie.                                   |
00041| | `toString()`                | String           | Returns a string representation of the cookies.                                 |
00042| 
00043| ### Options
00044| 
00045| When setting a cookie, the following properties from the `options` object are supported:
00046| 
00047| | Option        | Type                                   | Description                                                                        |
00048| | ------------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
00049| | `name`        | String                                 | Specifies the name of the cookie.                                                  |
00050| | `value`       | String                                 | Specifies the value to be stored in the cookie.                                    |
00051| | `expires`     | Date                                   | Defines the exact date when the cookie will expire.                                |
00052| | `maxAge`      | Number                                 | Sets the cookie’s lifespan in seconds.                                             |
00053| | `domain`      | String                                 | Specifies the domain where the cookie is available.                                |
00054| | `path`        | String, default: `'/'`                 | Limits the cookie's scope to a specific path within the domain.                    |
00055| | `secure`      | Boolean                                | Ensures the cookie is sent only over HTTPS connections for added security.         |
00056| | `httpOnly`    | Boolean                                | Restricts the cookie to HTTP requests, preventing client-side access.              |
00057| | `sameSite`    | Boolean, `'lax'`, `'strict'`, `'none'` | Controls the cookie's cross-site request behavior.                                 |
00058| | `priority`    | String (`"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`) | Specifies the cookie's priority                                                    |
00059| | `partitioned` | Boolean                                | Indicates whether the cookie is [partitioned](https://github.com/privacycg/CHIPS). |
00060| 
00061| The only option with a default value is `path`.
00062| 
00063| To learn more about these options, see the [MDN docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Cookies).
00064| 
00065| ## Good to know
00066| 
00067| - `cookies` is an **asynchronous** function that returns a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to access cookies.
00068|   - In version 14 and earlier, `cookies` was a synchronous function. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future.
00069| - `cookies` is a [Request-time API](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) whose returned values cannot be known ahead of time. Using it in a layout or page will opt a route into [dynamic rendering](/docs/app/glossary#dynamic-rendering).
00070| - With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), calling `cookies()` outside of a [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary prevents the route from being prerendered. See [Next.js encountered runtime data during prerendering](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-runtime) for fix options.
00071| - The `.delete` method can only be called:

## Usage

The [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive caches the return value of async functions and components. You can apply it at two levels:

- **Data-level**: Cache a function that fetches or computes data (e.g., `getProducts()`, `getUser(id)`)
- **UI-level**: Cache an entire component or page (e.g., `async function BlogPosts()`)

A cache directive gives a result a lifetime, which Next.js uses for time-based revalidation and rendering optimizations. For on-demand revalidation after a mutation, see [Revalidating](/docs/app/getting-started/revalidating). See [Prerendering](#prerendering) for how cached results become part of the static shell and may be included in a [prefetch](#prefetching).

> **Good to know:** We recommend pairing every cache directive with a [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife). Without one, the implicit `default` profile applies.
